title: Ascites-image models stratify recorded platinum resistance in ovarian cancer
summary: OVCAP analyzed pretreatment ascites cytology from 438 women with advanced epithelial ovarian cancer. Internal and two additional-site validation cohorts yielded resistance-classification AUCs of 0.894, 0.863 and 0.828. This retrospective treatment-response study does not establish that model-guided treatment improves outcomes.
ai_technology: Prov-GigaPath features, TransMIL and multi-scale late fusion
organization: Fudan University Shanghai Cancer Center; Northern Jiangsu People’s Hospital

source_review.scope: Original model/clinical cohort, outcome definition, patient-level training selection and held-out Results; exploratory biological interpretation and clinical benefit kept bounded.

evidence.tested: The 2019–2023 cohort comprised 367 Xuhui-campus cases split into 254 training and 113 internal-validation patients, plus 51 Pudong-campus and 20 Northern-Jiangsu validation patients. Patient-level three-fold training cross-validation selected among 15 encoders and hyperparameters. The retained multi-scale predictor was applied unchanged to the held-out cohorts. Resistance meant progression during therapy or recurrence/progression within six months after completing platinum treatment; the reported internal/external AUCs were .894/.863/.828.
evidence.unknown: The three sites represent two institutions; one additional-site cohort shares the same cancer center as development. The smallest cohort contains only 20 people. Retrospective selection of patients with evaluable outcomes, histologic concentration in high-grade serous cancer and preparation/scanner differences constrain transfer. AUCs are not treatment-benefit estimates. Attention-selected morphology and integrated single-cell associations are hypothesis-generating, not established mechanisms of resistance. Clinical vignettes and comparison with later-available kinetic biomarkers do not demonstrate prospective clinical utility.
evidence.ai_role: Pathology foundation-model embeddings and attention-based multiple-instance learning estimated response risk from image patches; trained multi-scale fusion combined the prediction streams.
